description: Hey! We are GammaRads. A group of radical people, ready to burst all bubbles and flood everyone with Gamma or so we think.
summary:
PYRO-SYNC (team GammaRads) is a web app that makes NASA's satellite fire hotspot record comparable across sensors. Since 2012, VIIRS (375 m) has joined MODIS (1 km), and raw hotspot counts jump simply because the newer sensor is more sensitive and splits one fire into several pixels. In our global NASA FIRMS totals, raw detection rows are about 4.7 times higher in 2012–2017 than in 2003–2011, while fire radiative power per active satellite is only about 1.14 times higher.

PYRO-SYNC groups detections into H3 hexagon cells, applies a sensitivity cutoff to each cell's total energy, divides by the number of active satellites, and scores each week against the same week in other years. The result is an interactive Burning Activity Calendar and map, with a Raw vs Harmonized toggle, for three benchmark regions (Punjab/Haryana, California, Amazon) and the world. Emergency responders, land managers and scientists can spot unusual fire weeks and study long-term patterns without the 2012 sensor break. Every number comes from deterministic code on real NASA FIRMS data.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

PYRO-SYNC turns 26 years of NASA active-fire hotspots (MODIS from 2000, VIIRS from 2012) into one comparable record and shows it as a burning activity calendar (weeks by years) linked to a map. Users pick a region or the world, switch between Raw and Harmonized views, click any week to see its hexagons, and jump to the strongest anomaly. A live mode shows the last 24 hours from the FIRMS API and falls back to cached archive data if the service is unavailable.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Detections are snapped to H3 hexagon cells and grouped by cell, day and satellite, so one fire split across several 375 m VIIRS pixels becomes one unit.

2. A sensitivity cutoff (default 2.0 MW, adjustable) is applied to the cell's total fire radiative power (FRP), not to single pixels, so VIIRS counts only fires MODIS could also see.

3. Weekly FRP is divided by the number of active satellites, so adding satellites does not inflate trends.

4. Each week is Z-scored against the same week in other years, and simple rules tag regimes (agricultural burn, wildfire front, static flare).

RESULT (global FIRMS totals)

Raw detection rows in 2012–2017 are about 4.65 times the 2003–2011 level. FRP per active satellite is about 1.14 times that level. The sensor step shrinks by most of its size, and a small residual remains that we have not yet explained (it could be real change, extra VIIRS energy the global total does not filter, or normal variation).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Responders and land managers can see whether a week is unusual compared with history. Scientists and policy makers get a record without a break at 2012. Heavy processing runs once offline, so the app loads small compressed files.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, H3) for cleaning and aggregation; Next.js, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, deck.gl, Recharts and h3-js for the app; Vitest for tests; Vercel for hosting.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

Instead of plotting raw dots, we compare energy per cell and satellite, and make the sensor break visible and removable with one toggle.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED AND LIMITS

The world map layer sums energy but does not apply the VIIRS cutoff; regional views do. Regime tags are unvalidated first-draft rules. Terra and Aqua are near end of life. Related tools such as Copernicus GWIS compare each sensor with its own recent average, and research on MODIS–VIIRS fusion is more rigorous than our first-order correction; our contribution is an accessible, interactive way to see one record across the sensor change.

AI USE

Code, scripts and text were written with AI assistance. All numbers are computed by deterministic code; no AI model calculates any value.

DATA ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

We acknowledge the use of data from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), part of NASA's Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS).
